## P3 - Hardcoded `clab-%s-%s` long-name derivation in `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` and destroy sweep diverges from `nodeLongName` under non-default `prefix`

**Location:** [core/apply&#95;bridge&#95;migration.go:40-47](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L40-L47)

**Problem:** `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` at [`core/apply_bridge_migration.go:40-47`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L40-L47) and the destroy sweep state entries at [`core/destroy.go:497-509`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L497-L509) derive a bridge node&#39;s container long name as `fmt.Sprintf("clab-%s-%s", ...)`, while the actual long name is produced by the prefix-aware helper `c.nodeLongName` at [`core/config.go:309-318`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/config.go#L309-L318), which yields `<lab>-<node>` for `prefix: __lab-name`, `<prefix>-<lab>-<node>` for a custom `prefix`, and the bare node name for an empty `prefix`. In the common bridge-move case the stale bridge node is intentionally absent from `c.Nodes`, so the hardcoded fallback in `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` is the primary derivation used to key parking netnses. Recovery on the next apply &#40;`recoverParkedBridgeNSPorts` via `ParkingNetnsName(node.Config().LongName)` at [`core/topology_reconcile.go:1098`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/topology_reconcile.go#L1098-L1098)&#41; and the destroy-time state sweep then compute a different key than parking used.

**Trigger:** Deploy a lab with `prefix: __lab-name` or a custom/empty `prefix`, move a bridge between parents &#40;`br01\|bp1` to `br01\|bp2`&#41;, and either interrupt the migration between park and restore or destroy after parking.

**Impact:** With non-default prefixes, an interrupted migration&#39;s parked port is not recovered on the next apply, so the client pair is deleted and recreated instead of migrated, silently degrading the migration feature to a full link teardown. Additionally, the destroy-time `SweepParkingNetnses` computes the wrong `ParkingNetnsName` for state-recorded nodes, leaving the bind-mounted parking netns on the host. Default-prefix &#40;`clab`&#41; deployments are unaffected because all derivations coincide.

**Suggested correction:** Route both derivations through `c.nodeLongName(nodeName)` from [`core/config.go:309`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/config.go#L309-L309), which reproduces the current default-prefix form exactly, and add a unit test exercising the fallback path with `prefix: __lab-name`.


## P4 - Empty parking netns leaks when the owner bridge leaves both the rendered topology and the lab state

**Location:** [core/apply&#95;bridge&#95;migration.go:49-64](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L49-L64)

**Problem:** The comment at [`core/apply_bridge_migration.go:49-64`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L49-L64) claims that parking entries abandoned by interrupted migrations are removed at destroy, and the destroy sweep enumerates both `c.Nodes` and `state.Topology.Nodes`. However, `UnlinkEmptyParkingNetNS` &#40;[`links/migration.go:324`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/links/migration.go#L324-L324)&#41; is only invoked from `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` &#40;[`core/apply_bridge_migration.go:124`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L124-L124)&#41;. If a migration is interrupted between park and restore and a subsequent successful apply removes the bridge node entirely, that apply rewrites the lab state without the bridge, so at destroy time neither sweep source can derive the owner&#39;s `ParkingNetnsName`.

**Trigger:** Interrupt a bridge move so the bridge-side veth half sits parked in the `clab-park-...` netns, then apply a topology revision that deletes the bridge node, then run `clab destroy` with the topology file.

**Impact:** An empty named network namespace &#40;bind mount&#41; persists on the host indefinitely. It is harmless to subsequent labs and requires an unlikely event sequence, so this is a host-hygiene leak only.

**Suggested correction:** Persist the parking netns name &#40;or the owner bridge&#39;s long name&#41; in `LabState` when parking so the destroy sweep can enumerate it, or extend the sweep to also match `clab-park-*` entries containing the lab name.


## P4 - Destroy-time leftover-container and parking-netns sweeps are not documented in [`docs/cmd/destroy.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/docs/cmd/destroy.md#L1-L1)

**Location:** [core/destroy.go:455-513](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L455-L513)

**Problem:** Destroy now deletes lab-labeled containers absent from the rendered topology via `deleteLeftoverLabContainers` at [`core/destroy.go:455`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L455-L455) and sweeps parking netnses for deploy nodes plus state-recorded nodes at [`core/destroy.go:485-513`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L485-L513). Neither user-visible behavior is reflected in [`docs/cmd/destroy.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/docs/cmd/destroy.md#L1-L1), even though the PR documents the related deploy and bridge-kind behavior in [`docs/cmd/deploy.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/docs/cmd/deploy.md#L1-L1) and [`docs/manual/kinds/bridge.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/docs/manual/kinds/bridge.md#L1-L1).

**Trigger:** A user reads [`docs/cmd/destroy.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/docs/cmd/destroy.md#L1-L1) to learn what `clab destroy -t <topology-file>` removes.

**Impact:** Users cannot rely on or predict the new cleanup behavior; they may continue doing full destroy/deploy cycles to clear leftover containers that destroy now removes automatically, or be surprised that lab-labeled containers absent from the supplied topology file are deleted.

**Suggested correction:** Add a short paragraph to [`docs/cmd/destroy.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/docs/cmd/destroy.md#L1-L1) describing both sweeps, mirroring the wording of the code comments at [`core/destroy.go:485-489`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L485-L489).


## Coverage

- Source-only review&#58; tests were not executed; all findings derive from reading the diff, surrounding callers, helpers, schemas, docs, and tests in the snapshot.
- `waitForParentContainer` in [`nodes/bridge/bridge.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L1-L1) polls some container statuses without a bound, but both deploy &#40;`waitForNodeDeployTarget`&#41; and apply &#40;`waitForApplyNetworkModeTarget`&#41; paths gate dependents on Running parents first, external parents are rejected by the `dp.Nodes` membership check, and `Stopped` parents error out, so the unbounded statuses are unreachable in practice; no finding raised.
- The `strings.Contains(name, "\|")` heuristics in `planDesertedBridgeDeviceRemovals` and state-link detection can only misfire on non-bridge nodes whose names contain `\|`; the schema already allowed `\|` at the merge base, but runtimes reject `\|` in container names so such nodes never deploy; the heuristic is safe in practice.
- Leftover-sweep name matching was verified against runtime normalization&#58; docker trims the leading `/` in `produceGenericContainerList` at [`runtime/docker/docker.go:1562-1566`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/runtime/docker/docker.go#L1562-L1566), and podman returns bare names, so `cont.Names[0]` matches `cfg.LongName`.
- The fd-handle usage in [`nodes/bridge/bridge.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/nodes/bridge/bridge.go#L1-L1)&#39;s `ExecFunction` and `GetNSPath` matches the existing `DefaultNode` precedent; the CLI process is short-lived, so impact is negligible.
- Owned-but-detached veth ends &#40;not mastered by the bridge&#41; are invisible to orphan discovery, which only collects interfaces with `MasterIndex == bridgeIndex`; this is a minor edge leak.
- Interface names longer than 15 characters skip migration &#40;logical vs kernel name comparison&#41; and fall back to delete/recreate, which is graceful.
- Test coverage is solid for planning logic &#40;[`core/topology_reconcile_migration_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/topology_reconcile_migration_test.go#L1-L1)&#41; and end-to-end flows &#40;smoke test `tests/01-smoke/34-bridge-ns-reconcile` covers move, parent drift, interrupted-recovery injection, bridge removal, and idempotency&#41;. Two gaps remain untested&#58; the destroy leftover-container sweep &#40;teardown uses `destroy --name`, which takes the `deleteContainersDirect` branch&#41; and any non-default `prefix` scenario, which is where the P3 finding lives.

<content>
1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

83: new file mode 100644
84: index 0000000..3e99945
85: --- /dev/null
86: +++ b/core/apply_bridge_migration.go
87: @@ -0,0 +1,279 @@
88: +package core
89: +
90: +import (
91: +	"context"
92: +	"fmt"
93: +	"strings"
94: +
95: +	"github.com/charmbracelet/log"
96: +	clablinks "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/links"
97: +	clabutils "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/utils"
98: +)
99: +
100: +// bridgeNSMigParentNode resolves the namespace host of a migrated bridge-side
101: +// endpoint. Stale refs carry either a live bridge node (resolved via the
102: +// topology) or the name-encoded <bridge>|<parent> form of a node that is
103: +// already removed from the desired topology.
104: +func (c *CLab) bridgeNSMigParentNode(ref applyEndpointRef) (clablinks.Node, error) {
105: +	if parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSParentNode(ref.key.node); err == nil {
106: +		return parentNode, nil
107: +	}
108: +	parts := strings.SplitN(ref.key.node, "|", 2)
109: +	if len(parts) != 2 {
110: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot resolve namespace host of bridge %q", ref.key.node)
111: +	}
112: +	node, exists := c.Nodes[parts[1]]
113: +	if !exists {
114: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
115: +			"bridge %q: parent container %q not found",
116: +			ref.key.node,
117: +			parts[1],
118: +		)
119: +	}
120: +	return node, nil
121: +}
122: +
123: +// bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName returns the long name of the bridge node that owns
124: +// the migration's stale endpoint: the desired node's configured long name when
125: +// the bridge is part of the topology, and the standard "clab-<lab>-<node>"
126: +// derivation for state-recovered bridges.
127: +func (c *CLab) bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName(mig *bridgeNSMigration) string {
128: +	if node, exists := c.Nodes[mig.staleRef.key.node]; exists {
129: +		if cfg := node.Config(); cfg != nil && cfg.LongName != "" {
130: +			return cfg.LongName
131: +		}
132: +	}
133: +	return fmt.Sprintf("clab-%s-%s", c.Config.Name, mig.staleRef.key.node)
134: +}
135: +
136: +// parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts parks bridge-side veth ends whose owning in-container
137: +// bridge was replaced by a bridge under a different parent (the move case).
138: +// The veth pair stays intact: only the parked half leaves the dying parent's
139: +// namespace, so the client-side end keeps its state untouched. Parking slots
140: +// are keyed by the owning bridge's long name, so an interrupted migration's
141: +// parked port stays attributable to its owner.
142: +//
143: +// State is modified incrementally: if an error occurs partway through,
144: +// previously parked ports remain parked and the apply fails without
145: +// invalidating their pairs. This is intentional; parking happens before any
146: +// node is deleted, so the pre-apply state stays intact. Recovery happens
147: +// automatically on the next apply: when the same move is planned again,
148: +// parking finds the port parked and resumes instead of failing (the park step
149: +// is idempotent), and when the next apply no longer plans the move,
150: +// recoverParkedBridgeNSPorts plans the parked port's restore. Ports no
151: +// desired link claims are swept from parking netnses at destroy.
152: +func (c *CLab) parkMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
153: +	ctx context.Context,
154: +	plan *applyPlan,
155: +) error {
156: +	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
157: +		return nil
158: +	}
159: +
160: +	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
161: +		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
162: +
163: +		if mig.relocation != nil {
164: +			continue
165: +		}
166: +
167: +		// The old bridge node may already be deleted from the desired topology
168: +		// (the move case); resolve its namespace host by the name-encoded
169: +		// parent suffix, falling back to the normal resolution.
170: +		parentNode, err := c.bridgeNSMigParentNode(mig.staleRef)
171: +		if err != nil {
172: +			return err
173: +		}
174: +
175: +		relocation, err := clablinks.ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
176: +			ctx,
177: +			parentNode,
178: +			mig.staleRef.key.node,
179: +			mig.staleRef.key.iface,
180: +			c.bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName(mig),
181: +		)
182: +		if err != nil {
183: +			return err
184: +		}
185: +
186: +		mig.relocation = relocation
187: +	}
188: +
189: +	return nil
190: +}
191: +
192: +// restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts moves parked bridge-side ends into the replacement
193: +// bridge's parent namespace after that container (and the bridge) exist again,
194: +// relabels the ownership altname to the replacement bridge node, and re-enslaves
195: +// the port to the bridge. The migrated link is filtered out of addedLinks so
196: +// deployLinks skips pair re-creation for it.
197: +func (c *CLab) restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts(
198: +	ctx context.Context,
199: +	plan *applyPlan,
200: +) error {
201: +	if plan == nil || len(plan.bridgeNSMigrations) == 0 {
202: +		return nil
203: +	}
204: +
205: +	// Parked halves of every migration keep their parking netns until this
206: +	// point; unlink those that ran out of ports even when a later restore
207: +	// fails, so successful migrations do not leak onto failed applies.
208: +	parkNSPaths := make(map[string]struct{})
209: +	defer func() {
210: +		for nsPath := range parkNSPaths {
211: +			if err := clablinks.UnlinkEmptyParkingNetNS(nsPath); err != nil {
212: +				log.Debug("failed to unlink empty parking netns",
213: +					"path", nsPath, "err", err)
214: +			}
215: +		}
216: +	}()
217: +
218: +	for i := range plan.bridgeNSMigrations {
219: +		mig := &plan.bridgeNSMigrations[i]
220: +
221: +		if mig.relocation == nil || plan.plannedLinkSet == nil {
222: +			continue
223: +		}
224: +
225: +		parkNSPaths[mig.relocation.ParkNSPath()] = struct{}{}
226: +
227: +		// Restore into the replacement bridge's parent namespace; the bridge
228: +		// node interfaces with the parent's ns through its GetNSPath override.
229: +		bridgeNode, exists := c.Nodes[mig.newKey.node]
230: +		if !exists {
231: +			return fmt.Errorf("bridge migration target %q not found", mig.newKey.node)
232: +		}
233: +
234: +		if err := mig.relocation.RestoreBridgePort(
235: +			ctx,
236: +			bridgeNode,
237: +			mig.newKey.node,
238: +			bridgeNSNameInNamespace(mig.newKey.node),
239: +			clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(mig.newKey.iface),
240: +		); err != nil {
241: +			return err
242: +		}
243: +
244: +		// The moved bridge can leave its device deserted in a surviving
245: +		// parent's namespace once all of its ports are restored elsewhere.
246: +		if mig.staleRef.key.node != mig.newKey.node {
247: +			c.collectDesertedBridgeDevice(plan, mig.staleRef.key.node)
248: +		}
249: +
250: +		// The migrated pair is complete end-to-end (the client-side end was
251: +		// never touched and the parked bridge-side half is restored and
252: +		// enslaved). Filter the corresponding replaced link out of addedLinks
253: +		// so endpoint removal and pair re-creation never touch it.
254: +		kept := plan.addedLinks[:0]

256: +			if clablinks.RuntimeEndpointsContainEndpoint(
257: +				link,

259: +				mig.newKey.iface,
260: +			) {
261: +				log.Info(
262: +					"Restored migrated bridge port",
263: +					"bridge",
264: +					mig.newKey.node,
265: +					"port",
266: +					mig.newKey.iface,
267: +				)

269: +			}
270: +			kept = append(kept, link)

272: +		plan.addedLinks = kept
273: +	}

277: +
278: +// collectDesertedBridgeDevice records a bridge device for removal from its
279: +// parent's namespace when the named in-container bridge has vacated it.
280: +// Recovery migrations (stale and desired claim identical) restore into the
281: +// owner and have no deserted side, so callers skip the record for them.
282: +// Deleted or recreated parents clear their namespaces themselves.
283: +func (c *CLab) collectDesertedBridgeDevice(plan *applyPlan, bridgeNodeName string) {
284: +	parentName := c.extractBridgeParentName(bridgeNodeName)
285: +	if parentName == "" {
286: +		return
287: +	}
288: +	if _, deleted := plan.deletedNodeSet[parentName]; deleted {
289: +		return
290: +	}
291: +	if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[parentName]; recreated {
292: +		return
293: +	}
294: +	// The recreated bridge keeps its kernel device name, so its replacement
295: +	// must not be deleted.
296: +	if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[bridgeNodeName]; recreated {
297: +		return
298: +	}
299: +
300: +	deviceName := bridgeNSNameInNamespace(bridgeNodeName)
301: +
302: +	for i := range plan.desertedBridgeDevices {
303: +		d := &plan.desertedBridgeDevices[i]
304: +		if d.parentName == parentName && d.deviceName == deviceName {
305: +			return
306: +		}
307: +	}
308: +
309: +	plan.desertedBridgeDevices = append(plan.desertedBridgeDevices, desertedBridgeDevice{
310: +		parentName: parentName,
311: +		deviceName: deviceName,
312: +	})
313: +}
314: +
315: +// planDesertedBridgeDeviceRemovals records the bridge devices of BridgeNS
316: +// nodes dropped from the desired topology, when their parent container keeps
317: +// running. No migration covers such removals: the bridge-side pair halves
318: +// die together with the removed client-side ends, which leaves the bridge
319: +// device behind as an empty husk in the parent. Runtime container names
320: +// reject "|", so a "<bridge>|<parent>"-shaped node name uniquely identifies
321: +// a BridgeNS node. Removed BridgeNS nodes never reach the container-based
322: +// deleted-node scan (no container, not desired), so the previously deployed
323: +// state's topology is their only reliable source of current identity.
324: +func (c *CLab) planDesertedBridgeDeviceRemovals(plan *applyPlan) {
325: +	for bridgeNodeName := range plan.deletedNodeSet {
326: +		if !strings.Contains(bridgeNodeName, "|") {
327: +			continue
328: +		}
329: +		c.collectDesertedBridgeDevice(plan, bridgeNodeName)
330: +	}
331: +
332: +	if plan.state == nil || plan.state.Topology == nil {
333: +		return
334: +	}
335: +	for bridgeNodeName := range plan.state.Topology.Nodes {
336: +		if _, desired := c.Nodes[bridgeNodeName]; desired {
337: +			continue
338: +		}
339: +		if _, deleted := plan.deletedNodeSet[bridgeNodeName]; deleted {
340: +			continue
341: +		}
342: +		if !strings.Contains(bridgeNodeName, "|") {
343: +			continue
344: +		}
345: +		c.collectDesertedBridgeDevice(plan, bridgeNodeName)
346: +	}
347: +}
348: +
349: +// removeDesertedBridgeDevices deletes the recorded deserted bridge devices
350: +// from their parents' namespaces, repairing the state left by bridge moves
351: +// and bridge-node removals whose parents keep running.
352: +func (c *CLab) removeDesertedBridgeDevices(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
353: +	for _, d := range plan.desertedBridgeDevices {
354: +		parentNode, exists := c.Nodes[d.parentName]
355: +		if !exists {
356: +			continue
357: +		}
358: +
359: +		if err := clablinks.RemoveDesertedBridge(ctx, parentNode, d.deviceName); err != nil {
360: +			log.Debug("Failed to remove deserted bridge device",
361: +				"bridge", d.deviceName, "parent", d.parentName, "err", err)
362: +		}
363: +	}
364: +
365: +	return nil
366: +}

961: +// getClientPeerFromNode extracts the client-side peer of the given bridge-side
962: +// endpoint from the live bridge node's endpoint links.
963: +func (c *CLab) getClientPeerFromNode(
964: +	bridgeKey applyEndpointKey,
965: +	node clablinks.Node,
966: +) applyEndpointKey {
967: +	for _, ep := range node.GetEndpoints() {
968: +		if ep == nil || ep.GetLink() == nil {
969: +			continue
970: +		}
971: +		veth, ok := ep.GetLink().(*clablinks.LinkVEth)
972: +		// Only consider the link that actually holds bridgeKey; a bridge node
973: +		// with multiple ports exposes one link per port.
974: +		if !ok || len(veth.Endpoints) != 2 {
975: +			continue
976: +		}
977: +		for i := range veth.Endpoints {
978: +			e := veth.Endpoints[i]
979: +			if e.GetNode() == nil ||
980: +				e.GetNode().GetShortName() != bridgeKey.node ||
981: +				e.GetIfaceName() != bridgeKey.iface {
982: +				continue
983: +			}
984: +			peer := veth.Endpoints[1-i]
985: +			if peer.GetNode() == nil {
986: +				return applyEndpointKey{}
987: +			}
988: +			return applyEndpointKey{
989: +				peer.GetNode().GetShortName(),
990: +				peer.GetIfaceName(),
991: +			}
992: +		}
993: +	}
994: +	return applyEndpointKey{}
995: +}

1013: +		return true

1143: +// bridge. Interfaces are discovered in the parent container's namespace and
1144: +// mapped to their logical endpoint names via ownership altnames, so no ordering
1145: +// dependency with the remote endpoints' discovery exists. Orphaned

1669:  
1670:  In the example above, the bridge `br01` is created inside the container namespace of the `bp1` node. The bridge will be named `br01` inside the `bp1` container and will have an interface `c1eth1` connected to it from the `c1` node.
1671:  
1672:  The extra `|<parent node>` suffix is used to distinguish the bridges and make them unique for containerlab, but this suffix will be dropped when the bridge is created inside the container namespace, so the bridge will still be named `br01` inside the `bp1` and `bp2` containers.
1673: +
1674: +### Reconciling in-container bridges with deploy
1675: +
1676: +When a topology deployed with an in-container bridge is re-applied with a modified definition, `deploy` reconciles bridge ports in place:
1677: +
1678: +- adding or removing a client to the bridge adds or removes the corresponding port without touching the other attached ports
1679: +- moving the bridge to another parent node (`br01|bp1` becomes `br01|bp2`) does not recreate the client links: the bridge-side veth ends are parked in a temporary `clab-park-*` network namespace, moved into the new parent's namespace and renamed to their logical port names, so the client-side interfaces keep their addresses and MAC addresses
1680: +- if an apply is interrupted after parking but before the port is restored, the next deploy resumes the migration from the parked port instead of failing, even when the next deploy no longer plans the move (for example, because it reverted the bridge change)
1681: +- removing the in-container bridge node from the topology removes its device together with its ports from the surviving parent's namespace during the same apply
1682: +
1683: +Ports whose client side is removed, recreated, or rewired in the same apply cannot keep their pair intact; containerlab falls back to deleting and recreating such links.

1794: +// BridgePortRelocation describes a bridge-side veth end parked out of one
1795: +// namespace while the in-container bridge hosting it was replaced (a bridge
1796: +// parent move). The veth pair stays intact across the namespace hops: the
1797: +// client-side end keeps its address and MAC, and the parked half carries its
1798: +// device state until it is restored into the replacement namespace.
1799: +type BridgePortRelocation struct {
1800: +	parkNSPath   string
1801: +	KernelName   string // kernel-side name while parked
1802: +	OldOwnerName string
1803: +	IfaceName    string
1804: +	LongName     string // replacement bridge node's long name; exercises the parking netns name
1805: +}
1806: +
1807: +// ParkBridgePortByOwnership finds the interface carrying the ownership altname
1808: +// of (ownerName, ifaceName) in src's namespace and parks it into the parking
1809: +// netns keyed by the owner bridge's long name. Keying by the owner (not the
1810: +// migration target) keeps a parked port attributable and resolvable even when
1811: +// the target bridge later leaves the lab's topologies, and matches the
1812: +// destroy-time sweep enumeration. The pair survives: only the parked half is
1813: +// relocated. Idempotent: if the port is already parked, returns the existing
1814: +// relocation.
1815: +func ParkBridgePortByOwnership(
1816: +	ctx context.Context,
1817: +	src Node,
1818: +	ownerName string,
1819: +	ifaceName string,
1820: +	ownerLongName string,
1821: +) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {
1822: +	parkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(ownerLongName))
1823: +	if err != nil {
1824: +		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create parking netns for migration: %w", err)
1825: +	}
1826: +
1827: +	relocation := &BridgePortRelocation{
1828: +		parkNSPath:   parkPath,
1829: +		OldOwnerName: ownerName,
1830: +		IfaceName:    ifaceName,
1831: +		LongName:     ownerLongName,
1832: +	}
1833: +
1834: +	// Idempotency: a previous apply may have parked the port and failed before
1835: +	// restoring it. If the parking netns already holds the port, reuse the
1836: +	// parked half so an interrupted migration resumes instead of aborting.
1837: +	kernelName, parked, err := parkedKernelNameFor(parkPath, ownerName, ifaceName)
1838: +	if err != nil {
1839: +		return nil, err
1840: +	}
1841: +	if parked {
1842: +		relocation.KernelName = kernelName
1843: +		log.Debug("bridge port already parked, resuming migration",
1844: +			"owner", ownerName, "iface", ifaceName,
1845: +			"kernelName", kernelName, "parkNS", parkPath)
1846: +		return relocation, nil
1847: +	}
1848: +
1849: +	parkErr := src.ExecFunction(ctx, func(_ ns.NetNS) error {
1850: +		link, err := findLinkByOwnershipAltName(ownerName, ifaceName)
1851: +		if err != nil {
1852: +			return err
1853: +		}
1854: +
1855: +		relocation.KernelName = link.Attrs().Name
1856: +
1857: +		if err := netlink.LinkSetDown(link); err != nil {
1858: +			log.Debug("failed to bring down interface while parking",
1859: +				"iface", link.Attrs().Name, "err", err)
1860: +		}
1861: +
1862: +		parkNs, nsErr := ns.GetNS(parkPath)
1863: +		if nsErr != nil {
1864: +			return nsErr
1865: +		}
1866: +		defer parkNs.Close()
1867: +
1868: +		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(parkNs.Fd()))
1869: +	})
1870: +	if parkErr != nil {
1871: +		if unlinkErr := clabutils.UnlinkNamedNetNS(parkPath); unlinkErr != nil {
1872: +			log.Debug("failed to clean up parking netns after park error",
1873: +				"path", parkPath, "err", unlinkErr)
1874: +		}
1875: +		return nil, parkErr
1876: +	}
1877: +
1878: +	return relocation, nil
1879: +}

1881: +// FindParkedBridgePortByOwnership reports whether a port carrying the
1882: +// ownership altname of (ownerName, ifaceName) is currently parked in the
1883: +// owner's parking netns and, when found, returns the relocation ready for
1884: +// restore. It creates and mutates nothing.
1885: +func FindParkedBridgePortByOwnership(
1886: +	ownerLongName, ownerName, ifaceName string,
1887: +) (*BridgePortRelocation, bool, error) {
1888: +	parkPath, err := clabutils.GetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(ownerLongName))

1903: +		IfaceName:    ifaceName,
1904: +		LongName:     ownerLongName,
1905: +	}, true, nil
1906: +}

1912: +func RemoveDesertedBridge(

1936: +		if err := netlink.LinkDel(bridgeLink); err != nil {
1937: +			return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove deserted bridge %q: %w", bridgeName, err)
1938: +		}

1940: +
1941: +		return nil
1942: +	})
1943: +}

1969: +		}

1972: +		return netlink.LinkSetNsFd(link, int(dstNs.Fd()))
1973: +	})

1976: +	}

2470: +		select {

2476: +				return nil
2477: +			}

3267: +// entries abandoned by an interrupted bridge-port migration or by a node that

3270: +func SweepParkingNetnses(longNames ...string) error {

245: func runtimeContainerLess(a, b clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {
246: 	// internal holders own the network namespace of the other containers in the group,
247: 	// so they sort first to be deleted last.
248: 	aInternal := a.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
249: 	bInternal := b.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] == "true"
250: 	if aInternal != bInternal {
251: 		return aInternal
252: 	}
253: 
254: 	aName := runtimeContainerNodeName(a)
255: 	bName := runtimeContainerNodeName(b)
256: 
257: 	aOrder := runtimeComponentSortOrder(aName)
258: 	bOrder := runtimeComponentSortOrder(bName)
259: 	if aOrder != bOrder {
260: 		return aOrder < bOrder
261: 	}
262: 
263: 	return aName < bName
264: }
265: 
266: func runtimeComponentSortOrder(name string) int {
267: 	idx := strings.LastIndex(name, "-")
268: 	if idx < 0 || idx == len(name)-1 {
269: 		return 0
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	slot := strings.ToUpper(name[idx+1:])
273: 	if len(slot) == 1 && slot[0] >= 'A' && slot[0] <= 'Z' {
274: 		return 100 - int(slot[0])
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	var n int
278: 	for _, r := range slot {
279: 		if r < '0' || r > '9' {
280: 			return 0
281: 		}
282: 		n = n*10 + int(r-'0')
283: 	}
284: 
285: 	return n
286: }

28: func netlinkFamily(ip netip.Addr) int {
29: 	if ip.Is4() {
30: 		return netlink.FAMILY_V4
31: 	}
32: 	if ip.Is6() {
33: 		return netlink.FAMILY_V6
34: 	}
35: 	return netlink.FAMILY_ALL
36: }

40: 	// Be conservative and keep the name comfortably within Linux NAME_MAX (255 bytes).
41: 	maxParkingNetnsNameLen = 200

44: // BridgeByName returns a *netlink.Bridge referenced by its name.
45: func BridgeByName(name string) (*netlink.Bridge, error) {
46: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(name)
47: 	if err != nil {
48: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("could not lookup %q: %v", name, err)
49: 	}
50: 	br, ok := l.(*netlink.Bridge)
51: 	if !ok {
52: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%q already exists but is not a bridge", name)
53: 	}
54: 	return br, nil
55: }

57: // LinkContainerNS creates a symlink for containers network namespace
58: // so that it can be managed by iproute2 utility.
59: func LinkContainerNS(nspath, containerName string) error {
60: 	CreateDirectory("/run/netns/", clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault)
61: 	dst := "/run/netns/" + containerName
62: 	if _, err := os.Lstat(dst); err == nil {
63: 		os.Remove(dst)
64: 	}
65: 	err := os.Symlink(nspath, dst)
66: 	if err != nil {
67: 		return err
68: 	}
69: 	return nil
70: }

72: // GenMac generates a random MAC address for a given OUI.
73: func GenMac(oui string) (net.HardwareAddr, error) {
74: 	buf := make([]byte, 3)
75: 	_, _ = rand.Read(buf)
76: 
77: 	hwa, err := net.ParseMAC(fmt.Sprintf("%s:%02x:%02x:%02x", oui, buf[0], buf[1], buf[2]))
78: 	return hwa, err
79: }

81: // DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes a network namespace and removes the symlink created by LinkContainerNS
82: // func.
83: func DeleteNetnsSymlink(n string) error {
84: 	log.Debug("Deleting netns symlink: ", n)
85: 	sl := fmt.Sprintf("/run/netns/%s", n)
86: 	err := os.Remove(sl)
87: 	if err != nil {
88: 		log.Debug("Failed to delete netns symlink by path:", sl)
89: 	}
90: 	return nil

93: // ParkingNetnsName returns the deterministic named-netns identifier used to park
94: // a container's dataplane interfaces while the container is stopped.
95: func ParkingNetnsName(containerName string) string {
96: 	name := parkingNetnsPrefix + containerName
97: 	if len(name) <= maxParkingNetnsNameLen {
98: 		return name
99: 	}
100: 
101: 	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(containerName))
102: 	suffix := hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:10]
103: 
104: 	// leave room for "-" + suffix
105: 	maxBaseLen := maxParkingNetnsNameLen - 1 - len(suffix)
106: 	if maxBaseLen < 1 {
107: 		return suffix
108: 	}
109: 
110: 	return name[:maxBaseLen] + "-" + suffix
111: }

113: // SweepParkingNetnses removes the parking netns entries of the given container
114: // long names. Destroyed labs have nothing left to migrate or restore, so
115: // entries abandoned by an interrupted bridge-port migration or by a node that
116: // was parked outside of the lab's topology are swept, their parked ports
117: // included. Long names of nodes that never parked are skipped silently.
118: func SweepParkingNetnses(longNames ...string) error {
119: 	var errs []error
120: 	for _, longName := range longNames {
121: 		if longName == "" {
122: 			continue
123: 		}
124: 
125: 		name := ParkingNetnsName(longName)
126: 		if _, err := GetNamedNetNS(name); err != nil {
127: 			continue
128: 		}
129: 
130: 		if err := netns.DeleteNamed(name); err != nil {
131: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf(
132: 				"failed to remove parking netns %q: %w", name, err,
133: 			))
134: 		}
135: 	}
136: 	return errors.Join(errs...)
137: }

139: // LinkIPs returns IPv4/IPv6 addresses assigned to a link referred by its name.
140: func LinkIPs(ln string) (v4addrs, v6addrs []netlink.Addr, err error) {
141: 	l, err := netlink.LinkByName(ln)
142: 	if err != nil {
143: 		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to lookup link %q: %w", ln, err)
144: 	}
145: 
146: 	v4addrs, err = netlink.AddrList(l, netlink.FAMILY_V4)
147: 	if err != nil {
148: 		return nil, nil, err
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	v6addrs, err = netlink.AddrList(l, netlink.FAMILY_V6)
152: 	if err != nil {
153: 		return nil, nil, err
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	return
157: }

159: // FirstLinkIPs returns string representation of the first IPv4/v6 address
160: // found for a link referenced by name.
161: func FirstLinkIPs(ln string) (v4, v6 string, err error) {
162: 	v4addrs, v6addrs, err := LinkIPs(ln)
163: 	if err != nil {
164: 		return
165: 	}
166:

171: 	if len(v6addrs) != 0 {

178: // GetLinksByNamePrefix returns a list of links whose name matches a prefix.
179: func GetLinksByNamePrefix(prefix string) ([]netlink.Link, error) {
180: 	// filtered list of interfaces
181: 	if prefix == "" {
182: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("prefix is not specified")
183: 	}
184: 	var fls []netlink.Link
185: 
186: 	ls, err := netlink.LinkList()
187: 	if err != nil {
188: 		return nil, err
189: 	}
190: 	for _, l := range ls {
191: 		if strings.HasPrefix(l.Attrs().Name, prefix) {
192: 			fls = append(fls, l)
193: 		}
194: 	}
195: 	if len(fls) == 0 {
196: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no links found by specified prefix %s", prefix)
197: 	}
198: 	return fls, nil
199: }

201: func GetRouteForIP(ip net.IP) (*rtnl.Route, error) {
202: 	conn, err := rtnl.Dial(nil)
203: 	if err != nil {
204: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("can't establish netlink connection: %s", err)
205: 	}
206: 	defer conn.Close()
207: 
208: 	r, err := conn.RouteGet(ip)
209: 
210: 	return r, err
211: }

213: func CreateNamedNetNS(name string) (string, error) {
214: 	nsPath := filepath.Join("/run/netns", name)
215: 
216: 	goruntime.LockOSThread()
217: 	defer goruntime.UnlockOSThread()
218: 
219: 	currentNS, err := netns.Get()
220: 	if err != nil {
221: 		return "", err
222: 	}
223: 	defer currentNS.Close()
224: 
225: 	defer func() {
226: 		_ = netns.Set(currentNS)
227: 	}()
228: 
229: 	newNS, err := netns.NewNamed(name)
230: 	if err != nil {
231: 		if os.IsExist(err) && FileOrDirExists(nsPath) {
232: 			return nsPath, nil
233: 		}
234: 		return "", err
235: 	}
236: 
237: 	newNS.Close()
238: 
239: 	return nsPath, nil
240: }

243: func CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(name string) (string, error) {
244: 	if nsPath, err := GetNamedNetNS(name); err == nil {
245: 		return nsPath, nil
246: 	}
247:

249: }

251: // GetNamedNetNS returns the nspath of the named netns, if it exists.
252: func GetNamedNetNS(name string) (string, error) {
253: 	nsPath := filepath.Join("/run/netns", name)
254: 	if !FileOrDirExists(nsPath) {
255: 		return "", fmt.Errorf("named netns %q does not exist", name)
256: 	}
257: 
258: 	return nsPath, nil
259: }
260: 
261: // UnlinkNamedNetNS removes the named netns symlink/mount.
262: // It umounts first (required for bind-mounted netns) then unlinks.
263: func UnlinkNamedNetNS(nsPath string) error {
264: 	if !FileOrDirExists(nsPath) {
265: 		return nil
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	// Unmount first (required for bind-mounted netns created by netns.NewNamed)
269: 	// Use MNT_DETACH to allow lazy unmount if the namespace is still in use.
270: 	if err := syscall.Unmount(nsPath, syscall.MNT_DETACH); err != nil {
271: 		// EOPNOTSUPP means it's not a mount point, which is fine
272: 		if err != syscall.EOPNOTSUPP && err != syscall.EINVAL {
273: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed to unmount netns %q: %w", nsPath, err)
274: 		}
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	return os.Remove(nsPath)
278: }
279: 
280: // SanitizeInterfaceName sanitizes the interface name by replacing '/' and ' ' with '-'.
281: // Making it suitable to write as AltName for the interface.
282: func SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName string) string {
283: 	var sb strings.Builder
284: 	sb.Grow(len(ifaceName))
285: 
286: 	for _, char := range ifaceName {
287: 		switch char {
288: 		case '/', ' ':
289: 			sb.WriteRune('-')
290: 		default:
291: 			sb.WriteRune(char)
292: 		}
293: 	}
294: 
295: 	return sb.String()
296: }

Reasoning
Confirmed the `runtimeNodeGroups` order-dependency bug: the loop over `c.Nodes` (map iteration, random order) checks `result[parentName]`, but the parent only gets into `result` if it was seen earlier in this same loop or via containers loop. Actually the first loop (containers) adds all container-backed nodes from labels, so parents (containers with labels) are added in the first loop! Parent containers exist at runtime and are listed via `ListContainers`, so `result[parentName]` exists from the first loop. So the BridgeNS branch is checking against the containers-derived groups, which are populated before the `c.Nodes` loop. So no ordering bug — parents are runtime containers and always in `result` from the first loop. Good, that's fine.

But wait: what if the parent container isn't running or doesn't exist? Then bridge not added → treated as new. That's correct behavior (parent gone → bridge gone).

Also note: `netns.DeleteNamed` — is that in the `github.com/vishvananda/netns` package? `DeleteNamed` exists in vishvananda/netns (added in v0.0.4+?). Actually vishvananda/netns doesn't have DeleteNamed historically... Let me check: vishvananda/netns has `NewNamed`, `GetNamed`, `DeleteNamed` — yes, recent versions have DeleteNamed. OK.

`UnlinkNamedNetNS` — fine.

Now `destroy.go` — need to read full destroy flow. And check `LoadState` signature and `LongName` derivation. Let me read destroy.go and check where `clab-<lab>-<node>` long name format is defined (constants or nodes naming).

28: func (c *CLab) Destroy(ctx context.Context, options ...DestroyOption) (err error) {
29: 	opts := NewDestroyOptions()
30: 
31: 	for _, opt := range options {
32: 		opt(opts)
33: 	}
34: 
35: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
36: 		return c.destroyWithLabRuntime(ctx, opts)
37: 	}
38: 
39: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
40: 
41: 	switch {
42: 	case opts.all:
43: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx)
44: 	case c.TopoPaths.TopologyFilenameAbsPath() != "":
45: 		containers, err = c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
46: 		if err == nil {
47: 			var tailscaleContainers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
48: 			tailscaleContainers, err = c.discoverTailscaleContainers(ctx, opts.nodeFilter)
49: 			containers = append(containers, tailscaleContainers...)
50: 		}
51: 	default:
52: 		var listOpts []ListOption
53: 
54: 		if c.Config.Name != "" {
55: 			listOpts = []ListOption{WithListLabName(c.Config.Name)}
56: 		} else {
57: 			listOpts = []ListOption{WithListclabLabelExists()}
58: 		}
59: 
60: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx, listOpts...)
61: 	}
62: 
63: 	if err != nil {
64: 		return err
65: 	}
66: 
67: 	// topo will hold the reference to the topology file
68: 	// as the key and the respective lab directory as the referenced value
69: 	topos := map[string]string{}
70: 
71: 	for idx := range containers {
72: 		topoFile, ok := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.TopoFile]
73: 		if !ok {
74: 			continue
75: 		}
76: 
77: 		topos[topoFile] = filepath.Dir(containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.NodeLabDir])
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	// failedLabDirs records the lab directories whose destroy failed or was never
81: 	// attempted. --cleanup keeps those directories: deleting the lab directory of
82: 	// a lab that is still running would discard the state file destroy needs for
83: 	// its management network cleanup on the next attempt.
84: 	failedLabDirs := map[string]bool{}
85: 
86: 	defer func() {
87: 		if opts.cleanup {
88: 			if cleanupErr := c.destroyLabDirs(topos, opts.all, failedLabDirs); cleanupErr != nil {
89: 				err = errors.Join(err, cleanupErr)
90: 			}
91: 		}
92: 	}()
93: 
94: 	if len(topos) == 0 {
95: 		return nil
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	log.Debugf("got the following topologies for destroy: %+v", topos)
99: 
100: 	// if all, and cli doesn't have --yes flag, and in a terminal -- prompt user confirmation
101: 	if opts.all && opts.terminalPrompt && term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdin.Fd())) {
102: 		err := cliPromptToDestroyAll(topos)
103: 		if err != nil {
104: 			return err
105: 		}
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	var errs []error
109: 
110: 	for topo, labDir := range topos {
111: 		cc, err := c.makeCopyForDestroy(ctx, topo, labDir, *opts)
112: 		if err != nil {
113: 			log.Errorf("error creating clab instance for topo %q: %v", topo, err)
114: 
115: 			errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf(
116: 				"error creating clab instance for topo %q: %w", topo, err))
117: 			failedLabDirs[labDir] = true
118: 
119: 			continue
120: 		}
121: 
122: 		err = cc.destroy(ctx, opts.maxWorkers, opts.keepMgmtNet)
123: 		if err != nil {
124: 			log.Errorf("Error occurred during the %s lab deletion: %v", cc.Config.Name, err)
125: 			errs = append(errs, err)
126: 			failedLabDirs[labDir] = true
127: 		}
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	if len(errs) != 0 {
131: 		return fmt.Errorf("error(s) occurred during the deletion. Check log messages")
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	return nil
135: }

137: // creates a mostly cloned version of the current c but set to the new topology, and with the
138: // necessary steps (mgmt network things) handled preparing the new CLab for destruction.
139: func (c *CLab) makeCopyForDestroy(
140: 	ctx context.Context,
141: 	topo,
142: 	labDir string,
143: 	opts DestroyOptions,
144: ) (*CLab, error) {
145: 	newOpts := []ClabOption{
146: 		WithTimeout(c.timeout),
147: 		// a topology edited after deploy may no longer pass the mgmt-net link checks,
148: 		// which must not prevent the removal of the deployed lab.
149: 		WithSkippedMgmtNetLinksCheck(),
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	// the copy must expand the topology with the same env vars as the deployment did
153: 	if c.topologyEnv != nil {
154: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithTopologyEnv(c.topologyEnv))
155: 	}
156: 
157: 	// Try to load topology file if it exists, otherwise use lab name only.
158: 	// This allows destroying labs even when the topology file has been deleted.
159: 	// WithTopoPath / WithLabNameOnly must run before WithNodeFilter so filterClabNodes
160: 	// sees topology nodes (see filterClabNodes in clab.go).
161: 	varsFiles := opts.varsFiles
162: 	if len(varsFiles) == 0 {
163: 		varsFiles = c.TopoPaths.VarsFilenamesAbsPath()
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	if clabutils.FileOrDirExists(topo) {
167: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithTopoPath(topo, varsFiles))
168: 	} else {
169: 		// Derive lab name from lab directory (format: clab-<labname>)
170: 		labName := filepath.Base(labDir)
171: 		labName = strings.TrimPrefix(labName, "clab-")
172: 		log.Debugf("topology file %q not found, using lab name %q for destroy", topo, labName)
173: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithLabNameOnly(labName))
174: 	}
175: 
176: 	newOpts = append(newOpts,
177: 		WithNodeFilter(opts.nodeFilter),
178: 		// during destroy we don't want to check bind paths
179: 		// as it is irrelevant for this command.
180: 		WithSkippedBindsPathsCheck(),
181: 		WithRuntime(
182: 			c.globalRuntimeName,
183: 			&clabruntime.RuntimeConfig{
184: 				Debug:            c.Config.Debug,
185: 				Timeout:          c.timeout,
186: 				GracefulShutdown: opts.graceful,
187: 			},
188: 		),
189: 	)
190: 
191: 	if opts.keepMgmtNet {
192: 		newOpts = append(newOpts, WithKeepMgmtNet())
193: 	}
194: 
195: 	cc, err := NewContainerLab(newOpts...)
196: 	if err != nil {
197: 		return nil, err
198: 	}
199: 	if labDir != "" && clabutils.FileOrDirExists(labDir) {
200: 		// adjust the labdir. Usually we take the PWD. but now on destroy time,
201: 		// we might be in a different Dir.
202: 		err = cc.TopoPaths.SetLabDir(labDir)
203: 		if err != nil {
204: 			return nil, err
205: 		}
206: 	}
207: 
208: 	// populate the management network state (bridge names) destroy needs for the
209: 	// removal of the iptables rules, without creating networks that are missing:
210: 	// a lab deployed with a management network override leaves the topology's
211: 	// default network uncreated, and creating it here would collide with the
212: 	// subnets the override is using.
213: 	if !cc.mgmtNetworksSkipped() {
214: 		var bridged clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
215: 		for _, m := range cc.allMgmtNetworks() {
216: 			if m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {
217: 				bridged = append(bridged, m)
218: 			}
219: 		}
220: 		if err = cc.resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(ctx, bridged); err != nil {
221: 			return nil, err
222: 		}
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	err = cc.setMgmtNetLinkBridges()
226: 	if err != nil {
227: 		return nil, err
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	err = cc.ResolveLinks()
231: 	if err != nil {
232: 		return nil, err
233: 	}
234: 
235: 	return cc, nil
236: }
237: 
238: // resolveExistingMgmtNetworks inspects the management networks that already exist
239: // so their bridge names are populated, e.g. for the iptables cleanup on destroy.
240: // Networks that do not exist are skipped: they hold no bridge yet, and the callers
241: // must not create management networks. Runtimes that cannot check network existence
242: // keep the create-or-inspect behavior.
243: func (c *CLab) resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(
244: 	ctx context.Context,
245: 	networks clabtypes.MgmtNetworks,
246: ) error {
247: 	var existing clabtypes.MgmtNetworks
248: 
249: 	for _, m := range networks {
250: 		rt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
251: 		if rtErr != nil {
252: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
253: 			log.Debug(
254: 				"Skipping management network resolution", "network", m.Network, "error", rtErr,
255: 			)
256: 			continue
257: 		}
258: 
259: 		checker, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtNetworkChecker)
260: 		if !ok {
261: 			existing = append(existing, m)
262: 			continue
263: 		}
264: 
265: 		exists, err := checker.MgmtNetworkExists(ctx)
266: 		if err != nil {
267: 			return err
268: 		}
269: 		if !exists {
270: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network that does not exist", "network", m.Network)
271: 			continue
272: 		}
273: 
274: 		existing = append(existing, m)
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	return c.createNetworks(ctx, existing)
278: }

280: // destroyLabDirs removes the lab directories of the destroyed labs. Directories
281: // recorded in failedLabDirs are kept: their labs are still running, and the
282: // directory holds the lab state a later destroy attempt relies on.
283: func (c *CLab) destroyLabDirs(
284: 	topos map[string]string,
285: 	all bool,
286: 	failedLabDirs map[string]bool,
287: ) error {
288: 	if len(topos) == 0 {
289: 		log.Info("no containerlab containers found")
290: 
291: 		if !all {
292: 			labDir := c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()
293: 			if labDir == "" {
294: 				// Try to infer the precise lab directory when TopologyLabDir is not set,
295: 				// e.g. destroy --name without topology file. Only look for an exact
296: 				// clab-<name> match, never a wildcard.
297: 				if c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != "" {
298: 					candidates := []string{}
299: 					if base := os.Getenv("CLAB_LABDIR_BASE"); base != "" {
300: 						candidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(base, "clab-"+c.Config.Name))
301: 					}
302: 					if c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
303: 						candidates = append(
304: 							candidates,
305: 							filepath.Join(c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileDir(), "clab-"+c.Config.Name),
306: 						)
307: 					} else {
308: 						if wd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil && wd != "" {
309: 							candidates = append(
310: 								candidates,
311: 								filepath.Join(wd, "clab-"+c.Config.Name),
312: 							)
313: 						}
314: 					}
315: 					for _, cand := range candidates {
316: 						if _, err := os.Stat(cand); err == nil {
317: 							labDir = cand
318: 							break
319: 						}
320: 					}
321: 					if labDir == "" {
322: 						log.Info(
323: 							"lab directory not found, nothing to clean",
324: 							"candidates",
325: 							candidates,
326: 						)
327: 						return nil
328: 					}
329: 				} else {
330: 					log.Info("lab directory not found, nothing to clean")
331: 					return nil
332: 				}
333: 			}
334: 
335: 			// Safety: only remove directories that look like a lab directory.
336: 			base := filepath.Base(labDir)
337: 			if !strings.HasPrefix(base, "clab-") {
338: 				log.Warnf("refusing to remove lab directory %q: unexpected name", labDir)
339: 				return nil
340: 			}
341: 			if c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != "" {
342: 				expected := "clab-" + c.Config.Name
343: 				if base != expected {
344: 					log.Warnf(
345: 						"refusing to remove lab directory %q: does not match expected %q",
346: 						labDir,
347: 						expected,
348: 					)
349: 					return nil
350: 				}
351: 			}
352: 
353: 			if _, err := os.Stat(labDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
354: 				log.Info("lab directory not found, nothing to clean", "path", labDir)
355: 				return nil
356: 			} else if err != nil {
357: 				log.Debug("failed to stat lab directory, skipping", "path", labDir, "error", err)
358: 				return nil
359: 			}
360: 
361: 			log.Info("Removing lab directory", "path", labDir)
362: 			if err := os.RemoveAll(labDir); err != nil {
363: 				log.Errorf("error deleting lab directory: %v", err)
364: 				return err
365: 			}
366: 		}
367: 
368: 		return nil
369: 	}
370: 
371: 	for _, labdir := range topos {
372: 		if failedLabDirs[labdir] {
373: 			log.Warnf(
374: 				"keeping lab directory %s: the lab was not destroyed, so its state is kept for a later attempt",
375: 				labdir,
376: 			)
377: 
378: 			continue
379: 		}
380: 
381: 		err := os.RemoveAll(labdir)
382: 		if err != nil {
383: 			log.Errorf("error deleting lab directory: %v", err)
384: 		}
385: 	}
386: 
387: 	return nil
388: }

390: func (c *CLab) destroy(ctx context.Context, maxWorkers uint, keepMgmtNet bool) error {
391: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
392: 	var orphanSidecars []clabruntime.GenericContainer
393: 	var err error
394: 
395: 	// If we have nodes defined (from topology file), list containers by node.
396: 	// Otherwise, list containers by lab name label (for destroy-by-name-only case).
397: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
398: 		containers, err = c.ListNodesContainersIgnoreNotFound(ctx)
399: 	} else if c.Config.Name != "" {
400: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx, WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
401: 	}
402: 
403: 	if err != nil {
404: 		return err
405: 	}
406: 
407: 	if len(c.Nodes) == 0 {
408: 		c.addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers)
409: 	}
410: 
411: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
412: 		tailscaleContainers, err := c.discoverTailscaleContainers(ctx, c.nodeFilter)
413: 		if err != nil {
414: 			return err
415: 		}
416: 		for _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {
417: 			if _, desired := c.Nodes[ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeName]]; desired {
418: 				continue
419: 			}
420: 			containers = append(containers, ctr)
421: 			if ctr.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] == "" {
422: 				orphanSidecars = append(orphanSidecars, ctr)
423: 			}
424: 		}
425: 	}
426: 
427: 	if len(containers) == 0 {
428: 		if len(c.Nodes) > 0 && len(c.Links) > 0 {
429: 			c.deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)
430: 		}
431: 		return nil
432: 	}
433: 
434: 	if maxWorkers == 0 {
435: 		maxWorkers = uint(len(containers))
436: 	}
437: 
438: 	log.Info("Destroying lab", "name", c.Config.Name)
439: 
440: 	// If we have nodes defined, use the normal node-based deletion.
441: 	// Otherwise, delete containers directly via the runtime (for destroy-by-name-only case).
442: 	if len(c.Nodes) > 0 {
443: 		c.preDestroyNodes(ctx, slices.Collect(maps.Values(c.Nodes)), maxWorkers)
444: 
445: 		err := clablinks.CleanupFilteredLinks(
446: 			ctx,
447: 			c.Config.Topology.Links,
448: 			c.Config.Name,
449: 			c.nodeFilter,
450: 		)
451: 		if err != nil {
452: 			return err
453: 		}
454: 		c.deleteNodes(ctx, maxWorkers)
455: 		c.deleteLeftoverLabContainers(ctx)
456: 		c.deleteContainersDirect(ctx, orphanSidecars)
457: 	} else {
458: 		c.deleteContainersDirect(ctx, containers)
459: 	}
460: 
461: 	c.deleteToolContainers(ctx)
462: 
463: 	log.Info("Removing host entries", "path", "/etc/hosts")
464: 
465: 	err = c.DeleteEntriesFromHostsFile()
466: 	if err != nil {
467: 		return fmt.Errorf("error while trying to clean up the hosts file: %w", err)
468: 	}
469: 
470: 	log.Info("Removing SSH config", "path", c.TopoPaths.SSHConfigPath())
471: 
472: 	err = c.RemoveSSHConfig(c.TopoPaths)
473: 	if err != nil {
474: 		log.Errorf("failed to remove ssh config file: %v", err)
475: 	}
476: 
477: 	// delete container network namespaces symlinks
478: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
479: 		err = node.DeleteNetnsSymlink()
480: 		if err != nil {
481: 			return fmt.Errorf("error while deleting netns symlinks: %w", err)
482: 		}
483: 	}
484: 
485: 	// Sweep this lab's leftover parking netns entries. Destroyed labs have
486: 	// nothing left to migrate or restore, so entries abandoned by an
487: 	// interrupted bridge-port migration are removed, parked ports included.
488: 	// Candidates are the deploy nodes plus every node recorded in the lab
489: 	// state, so slots of bridges that left the topology still get swept.
490: 	longNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Nodes))
491: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
492: 		if cfg := node.Config(); cfg != nil {
493: 			longNames = append(longNames, cfg.LongName)
494: 		}
495: 	}
496: 
497: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
498: 	switch {
499: 	case err != nil:
500: 		// Mirror the management-network cleanup wording; a missing state only
501: 		// narrows the sweep to the current topology's nodes.
502: 		log.Debug("Unable to load the parking netns entries recorded in the lab state", "error", err)
503: 	case state != nil && state.Topology != nil:
504: 		// Slots of nodes that left the topology since the last deploy still
505: 		// get swept through the recorded state.
506: 		for nodeName := range state.Topology.Nodes {
507: 			longNames = append(longNames, fmt.Sprintf("clab-%s-%s", c.Config.Name, nodeName))
508: 		}
509: 	}
510: 
511: 	if err := clabutils.SweepParkingNetnses(longNames...); err != nil {
512: 		log.Warnf("failed to clean up parking namespaces: %v", err)
513: 	}
514: 
515: 	// delete every defined management network, including extra networks
516: 	// that apply may have left without nodes, and networks a previous
517: 	// deployment recorded in the lab state but the topology no longer defines
518: 	for _, m := range c.mgmtNetworksForCleanup() {
519: 		if m.Network == "bridge" || keepMgmtNet {
520: 			continue
521: 		}
522: 		log.Debugf("Calling DeleteNet method. Management network value is: %+v", m)
523: 
524: 		rt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)
525: 		if rtErr != nil {
526: 			// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks
527: 			log.Debug("Skipping management network deletion", "network", m.Network, "error", rtErr)
528: 			continue

530: 		if err = rt.DeleteNet(ctx); err != nil {
531: 			switch {
532: 			case err.Error() == fmt.Sprintf("Error: No such network: %s", m.Network):
533: 			case strings.Contains(err.Error(), fmt.Sprintf(" network %s not found", m.Network)):
534: 			default:
535: 				log.Error(err)
536: 			}
537: 		}
538: 	}
539: 
540: 	return nil
541: }

543: func (c *CLab) addMgmtNetworksFromContainers(containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer) {
544: 	for _, ctr := range containers {
545: 		switch name := ctr.NetworkName; name {
546: 		case "", "unknown", "bridge", "host", "none":
547: 		default:
548: 			if c.mgmtNetByNetwork(name).Network == name {
549: 				continue
550: 			}
551: 			c.Config.MgmtNetworks = append(c.Config.MgmtNetworks, &clabtypes.MgmtNet{
552: 				Network:        name,
553: 				Bridge:         ctr.Labels[clabconstants.NodeMgmtNetBr],
554: 				ExternalAccess: new(true),
555: 			})
556: 		}
557: 	}

560: // mgmtNetworksForCleanup returns the management networks to delete on destroy:
561: // the topology-defined ones plus any network a previous deployment recorded in
562: // the lab state but that the current topology no longer defines. Without the
563: // state record a network dropped from the mgmt list would never be removed.
564: func (c *CLab) mgmtNetworksForCleanup() clabtypes.MgmtNetworks {
565: 	networks := c.allMgmtNetworks()
566: 
567: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
568: 	if err != nil {
569: 		log.Warn("Unable to load the management networks recorded in the lab state", "error", err)
570: 		return networks
571: 	}
572: 	if state == nil {
573: 		return networks
574: 	}
575: 
576: 	defined := make(map[string]bool, len(networks))
577: 	for _, m := range networks {
578: 		defined[m.Network] = true
579: 	}
580: 	for _, name := range state.MgmtNetworks {
581: 		if defined[name] {
582: 			continue
583: 		}
584: 		defined[name] = true
585: 		// ExternalAccess mirrors the default every management network gets, so
586: 		// the forwarding rule installed for the network is cleaned up too.
587: 		networks = append(networks, &clabtypes.MgmtNet{
588: 			Network:        name,
589: 			ExternalAccess: new(true),
590: 		})
591: 	}
592: 
593: 	return networks
594: }

596: func (c *CLab) deleteApplyNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
597: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(plan.deletedNodeSet)+len(plan.recreatedNodeSet))
598: 	for nodeName := range plan.deletedNodeSet {
599: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
600: 	}
601: 	for nodeName := range plan.recreatedNodeSet {
602: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
603: 	}
604: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
605: 
606: 	hookNodes := make([]clabnodes.Node, 0, len(nodeNames))
607: 	var tailscaleContainers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
608: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
609: 		runtimeNode := plan.currentNodes[nodeName]
610: 		if runtimeNode == nil {
611: 			return fmt.Errorf("runtime node %q not found", nodeName)
612: 		}
613: 		if runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {
614: 			continue
615: 		}
616: 		if len(runtimeNode.containers) > 0 &&
617: 			runtimeNode.containers[0].Labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] == clabnodestailscale.KindName {
618: 			tailscaleContainers = append(tailscaleContainers, runtimeNode.containers...)
619: 			continue
620: 		}
621: 		if node, ok := c.Nodes[nodeName]; ok {
622: 			hookNodes = append(hookNodes, node)
623: 		}
624: 	}
625: 	var logoutWg sync.WaitGroup
626: 	for _, ctr := range tailscaleContainers {
627: 		logoutWg.Go(func() { c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, ctr) })
628: 	}
629: 	c.preDestroyNodes(ctx, hookNodes, 0)
630: 	logoutWg.Wait()
631: 
632: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
633: 		runtimeNode := plan.currentNodes[nodeName]
634: 		if runtimeNode.external || runtimeNode.rootNamespaceBased {
635: 			continue
636: 		}
637: 
638: 		for i := len(runtimeNode.containers) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
639: 			ctr := runtimeNode.containers[i]
640: 			if len(ctr.Names) == 0 {
641: 				return fmt.Errorf("runtime container for node %q has no name", nodeName)
642: 			}
643: 
644: 			runtime := ctr.Runtime
645: 			if runtime == nil {
646: 				runtime = c.globalRuntime()
647: 			}
648: 
649: 			action := "Deleting node"
650: 			if _, recreate := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreate {
651: 				action = "Deleting node for recreate"
652: 			}
653: 			log.Info(action, "node", nodeName, "container", ctr.Names[0])
654: 			if err := runtime.DeleteContainer(ctx, ctr.Names[0]); err != nil {
655: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed deleting node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
656: 			}
657: 
658: 			_ = clabutils.DeleteNetnsSymlink(ctr.Names[0])
659: 		}
660: 	}
661: 
662: 	return nil
663: }

665: // preDestroyNodes runs the PreDestroy stage of the given nodes concurrently, before any of them
666: // is deleted. Nodes without a container are skipped. A workers value of 0 runs all hooks at once.
667: func (*CLab) preDestroyNodes(ctx context.Context, nodes []clabnodes.Node, workers uint) {
668: 	if workers == 0 || workers > uint(len(nodes)) {
669: 		workers = uint(len(nodes))
670: 	}
671: 
672: 	sem := make(chan struct{}, workers)
673: 	wg := new(sync.WaitGroup)
674: 
675: 	for _, n := range nodes {
676: 		wg.Add(1)
677: 		sem <- struct{}{}
678: 
679: 		go func() {
680: 			defer wg.Done()
681: 			defer func() { <-sem }()
682: 
683: 			if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound {
684: 				return
685: 			}
686: 
687: 			if err := n.PreDestroy(ctx); err != nil {
688: 				log.Warnf("node %q pre-destroy hook failed: %v", n.Config().ShortName, err)
689: 			}
690: 		}()
691: 	}
692: 
693: 	wg.Wait()
694: }

696: func (c *CLab) deleteNodes(ctx context.Context, workers uint) {
697: 	wg := new(sync.WaitGroup)
698: 
699: 	concurrentChan := make(chan clabnodes.Node)
700: 
701: 	workerFunc := func(i uint, input chan clabnodes.Node, wg *sync.WaitGroup) {
702: 		defer wg.Done()
703: 
704: 		for {
705: 			select {
706: 			case n := <-input:
707: 				if n == nil {
708: 					log.Debugf("Worker %d terminating...", i)
709: 					return
710: 				}
711: 
712: 				err := n.Delete(ctx)
713: 				if err != nil {
714: 					log.Errorf("could not remove container %q: %v", n.Config().LongName, err)
715: 				}
716: 			case <-ctx.Done():
717: 				return
718: 			}
719: 		}
720: 	}
721: 
722: 	// start concurrent workers
723: 	wg.Add(int(workers))
724: 
725: 	for i := range workers {
726: 		go workerFunc(i, concurrentChan, wg)
727: 	}
728: 
729: 	// send nodes to workers
730: 	for _, n := range c.Nodes {
731: 		concurrentChan <- n
732: 	}
733: 
734: 	// close channel to terminate the workers
735: 	close(concurrentChan)
736: 
737: 	wg.Wait()
738: 
739: 	// Host and mgmt-br links must be removed only after node workers finish.
740: 	// vxlan-stitch teardown deletes veth pairs from containers concurrently with
741: 	// host-namespace VXLAN interfaces; running both at once races netlink deletes.
742: 	c.deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx)
743: }
744: 
745: func (c *CLab) deleteSpecialLinkNodes(ctx context.Context) {
746: 	specialNodes := append(
747: 		[]clablinks.Node{clablinks.GetHostLinkNode()},
748: 		clablinks.GetMgmtBrLinkNodes()...,
749: 	)
750: 	for _, n := range specialNodes {
751: 		err := n.Delete(ctx)
752: 		if err != nil {
753: 			log.Warn(err)
754: 		}
755: 	}
756: }

758: // deleteContainersDirect deletes containers directly via the runtime API.
759: // This is used when we don't have node objects (e.g., destroy-by-name-only case).
760: func (c *CLab) deleteContainersDirect(
761: 	ctx context.Context,
762: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
763: ) {
764: 	for _, cont := range containers {
765: 		if len(cont.Names) == 0 {
766: 			log.Warnf("skipping container %s with no names", cont.ID)
767: 			continue
768: 		}
769: 		name := cont.Names[0]
770: 		log.Infof("Removing container: %s", name)
771: 
772: 		c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, cont)
773: 		rt := cont.Runtime
774: 		if rt == nil {
775: 			rt = c.globalRuntime()
776: 		}
777: 		err := rt.DeleteContainer(ctx, name)
778: 		if err != nil {
779: 			log.Errorf("could not remove container %q: %v", name, err)
780: 		}
781: 	}
782: }

784: // deleteLeftoverLabContainers removes containers labeled for this lab whose
785: // node is not part of the rendered topology. Deployments made with different
786: // template variables, or nodes removed from the topology since, leave such
787: // containers behind: topology-based destroy only deletes nodes of the rendered
788: // node set, so these leftovers would survive every destroy otherwise.
789: //
790: // The sweep is skipped for node-filtered destroys (the filter deliberately
791: // keeps non-selected nodes; nothing outside the filtered set may be removed)
792: // and for tool containers (they are the deleteToolContainers flow's own
793: // responsibility).
794: func (c *CLab) deleteLeftoverLabContainers(ctx context.Context) {
795: 	if len(c.nodeFilter) > 0 {
796: 		log.Debug("Skipping lab leftover sweeps: destroy is node-filtered; non-selected containers must be preserved")
797: 		return
798: 	}
799: 
800: 	containers, err := c.ListContainers(ctx, WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
801: 	if err != nil {
802: 		log.Warnf("Failed to list containers for the lab leftover sweep: %v", err)
803: 		return
804: 	}
805: 
806: 	ownedByTopology := make(map[string]struct{}, len(c.Nodes))
807: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
808: 		if cfg := node.Config(); cfg != nil {
809: 			ownedByTopology[cfg.LongName] = struct{}{}
810: 		}
811: 	}
812: 
813: 	rt := c.globalRuntime()
814: 
815: 	for _, cont := range containers {
816: 		if len(cont.Names) == 0 {
817: 			continue
818: 		}
819: 		if _, owned := ownedByTopology[cont.Names[0]]; owned {
820: 			continue
821: 		}
822: 		if cont.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] != "" {
823: 			continue
824: 		}
825: 
826: 		log.Warnf("Removing leftover container %q; its node is not part of the rendered topology",
827: 			cont.Names[0])
828: 
829: 		if err := rt.DeleteContainer(ctx, cont.Names[0]); err != nil {
830: 			log.Errorf("could not remove leftover container %q: %v", cont.Names[0], err)
831: 		}
832: 	}
833: }

835: func (c *CLab) deleteToolContainers(ctx context.Context) {
836: 	toolTypes := []string{"sshx", "gotty"}
837: 	if len(c.nodeFilter) == 0 {
838: 		toolTypes = append(toolTypes, clabnodestailscale.ToolType)
839: 	}
840: 
841: 	for _, toolType := range toolTypes {
842: 		toolFilter := []*clabtypes.GenericFilter{
843: 			{
844: 				FilterType: "label",
845: 				Field:      clabconstants.ToolType,
846: 				Operator:   "=",
847: 				Match:      toolType,
848: 			},
849: 			{
850: 				FilterType: "label",
851: 				Field:      clabconstants.Containerlab,
852: 				Operator:   "=",
853: 				Match:      c.Config.Name,
854: 			},
855: 		}
856: 
857: 		containers, err := c.globalRuntime().ListContainers(ctx, toolFilter)
858: 		if err != nil {
859: 			log.Error("Failed to list tool containers", "tool", toolType, "error", err)
860: 			continue
861: 		}
862: 
863: 		if len(containers) == 0 {
864: 			log.Debug("No tool containers found for lab", "tool", toolType, "lab", c.Config.Name)
865: 			continue
866: 		}
867: 
868: 		log.Info("Found tool containers associated with a lab", "tool", toolType, "lab",
869: 			c.Config.Name, "count", len(containers))
870: 
871: 		for idx := range containers {
872: 			containerName := strings.TrimPrefix(containers[idx].Names[0], "/")
873: 
874: 			log.Info("Removing tool container", "tool", toolType, "container", containerName)
875: 
876: 			c.logoutTailscaleContainer(ctx, containers[idx])
877: 			if err := c.globalRuntime().DeleteContainer(ctx, containerName); err != nil {
878: 				log.Error("Failed to remove tool container", "tool", toolType,
879: 					"container", containerName, "error", err)
880: 			} else {
881: 				log.Info(
882: 					"Tool container removed successfully",
883: 					"tool",
884: 					toolType,
885: 					"container",
886: 					containerName,
887: 				)
888: 			}
889: 		}
890: 	}
891: }

893: func cliPromptToDestroyAll(topos map[string]string) error {
894: 	var sb strings.Builder
895: 
896: 	idx := 1
897: 
898: 	for topo, labDir := range topos {
899: 		sb.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("  %d. Topology: %s\n     Lab Dir: %s\n", idx, topo, labDir))
900: 		idx++
901: 	}
902: 
903: 	log.Warn("The following labs will be removed:", "labs", sb.String())
904: 
905: 	// red color (ansi code 1)
906: 	warningStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Bold(true).Foreground(lipgloss.Color("1"))
907: 	prompt := "Are you sure you want to remove all labs listed above? Enter 'y'," +
908: 		" to confirm or ENTER to abort: "
909: 	fmt.Print(warningStyle.Render(prompt))
910: 
911: 	reader := bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin)
912: 
913: 	input, err := reader.ReadString('\n')
914: 	if err != nil {
915: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to read user input: %v", err)
916: 	}
917: 
918: 	answer := strings.TrimSpace(input)
919: 	if answer == "" {
920: 		return errors.New("aborted by the user. No labs were removed")
921: 	}
922: 
923: 	answer = strings.ToLower(answer)
924: 	if answer != "y" && answer != "yes" {
925: 		return errors.New("aborted by the user. No labs were removed")
926: 	}
927: 
928: 	return nil
929: }

Usually we take the PWD. but now on destroy time,\n201: \t\t// we might be in a different Dir.\n202: \t\terr = cc.TopoPaths.SetLabDir(labDir)\n203: \t\tif err != nil {\n204: \t\t\treturn nil, err\n205: \t\t}\n206: \t}\n207: \n208: \t// populate the management network state (bridge names) destroy needs for the\n209: \t// removal of the iptables rules, without creating networks that are missing:\n210: \t// a lab deployed with a management network override leaves the topology's\n211: \t// default network uncreated, and creating it here would collide with the\n212: \t// subnets the override is using.\n213: \tif !cc.mgmtNetworksSkipped() {\n214: \t\tvar bridged clabtypes.MgmtNetworks\n215: \t\tfor _, m := range cc.allMgmtNetworks() {\n216: \t\t\tif m.Driver != clabtypes.MgmtDriverMacvlan {\n217: \t\t\t\tbridged = append(bridged, m)\n218: \t\t\t}\n219: \t\t}\n220: \t\tif err = cc.resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(ctx, bridged); err != nil {\n221: \t\t\treturn nil, err\n222: \t\t}\n223: \t}\n224: \n225: \terr = cc.setMgmtNetLinkBridges()\n226: \tif err != nil {\n227: \t\treturn nil, err\n228: \t}\n229: \n230: \terr = cc.ResolveLinks()\n231: \tif err != nil {\n232: \t\treturn nil, err\n233: \t}\n234: \n235: \treturn cc, nil\n236: }\n237: \n238: // resolveExistingMgmtNetworks inspects the management networks that already exist\n239: // so their bridge names are populated, e.g. for the iptables cleanup on destroy.\n240: // Networks that do not exist are skipped: they hold no bridge yet, and the callers\n241: // must not create management networks. Runtimes that cannot check network existence\n242: // keep the create-or-inspect behavior.\n243: func (c *CLab) resolveExistingMgmtNetworks(\n244: \tctx context.Context,\n245: \tnetworks clabtypes.MgmtNetworks,\n246: ) error {\n247: \tvar existing clabtypes.MgmtNetworks\n248: \n249: \tfor _, m := range networks {\n250: \t\trt, rtErr := c.mgmtRuntime(c.globalRuntimeName, m)\n251: \t\tif rtErr != nil {\n252: \t\t\t// runtimes without multiple network support never created extra networks\n253: \t\t\tlog.Debug(\n254: \t\t\t\t\"Skipping management network resolution\", \"network\", m.Network, \"error\", rtErr,\n255: \t\t\t)\n256: \t\t\tcontinue\n257: \t\t}\n258: \n259: \t\tchecker, ok := rt.(clabruntime.MgmtNetworkChecker)\n260: \t\tif !ok {\n261: \t\t\texisting = append(existing, m)\n262: \t\t\tcontinue\n263: \t\t}\n264: \n265: \t\texists, err := checker.MgmtNetworkExists(ctx)\n266: \t\tif err != nil {\n267: \t\t\treturn err\n268: \t\t}\n269: \t\tif !exists {\n270: \t\t\tlog.Debug(\"Skipping management network that does not exist\", \"network\", m.Network)\n271: \t\t\tcontinue\n272: \t\t}\n273: \n274: \t\texisting = append(existing, m)\n275: \t}\n276: \n277: \treturn c.createNetworks(ctx, existing)\n278: }\n279: \n280: // destroyLabDirs removes the lab directories of the destroyed labs. Directories\n281: // recorded in failedLabDirs are kept: their labs are still running, and the\n282: // directory holds the lab state a later destroy attempt relies on.\n283: func (c *CLab) destroyLabDirs(\n284: \ttopos map[string]string,\n285: \tall bool,\n286: \tfailedLabDirs map[string]bool,\n287: ) error {\n288: \tif len(topos) == 0 {\n289: \t\tlog.Info(\"no containerlab containers found\")\n290: \n291: \t\tif !all {\n292: \t\t\tlabDir := c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()\n293: \t\t\tif labDir == \"\" {\n294: \t\t\t\t// Try to infer the precise lab directory when TopologyLabDir is not set,\n295: \t\t\t\t// e.g. destroy --name without topology file. Only look for an exact\n296: \t\t\t\t// clab-<name> match, never a wildcard.\n297: \t\t\t\tif c.Config != nil && c.Config.Name != \"\" {\n298: \t\t\t\t\tcandidates := []string{}\n299: \t\t\t\t\tif base := os.Getenv(\"CLAB_LABDIR_BASE\"); base != \"\" {\n300: \t\t\t\t\t\tcandidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(base, \"clab-\"+c.Config.Name))\n301: \t\t\t\t\t}\n302: \t\t\t\t\tif
