        "text": "# destroy command\n\n### Description\n\nThe `destroy` command destroys a lab referenced by its [topology definition file](../manual/topo-def-file.md).\n\n--8<-- \"docs/cmd/deploy.md:env-vars-flags\"\n\n### Usage\n\n`containerlab [global-flags] destroy [local-flags]`\n\n**aliases:** `des`\n\n### Flags\n\n#### topology\n\nWith the global `--topo | -t` flag a user sets the path to the topology definition file that will be used to identify the lab to destroy.\n\nWhen the topology path refers to a directory, containerlab will look for a file with `.clab.yml` extension in that directory and use it as a topology definition file.\n\nWhen the topology file flag is omitted, containerlab will try to find the matching file name by looking at the current working directory.\n\nIf more than one file is found for directory-based path or when the flag is omitted entirely, containerlab will fail with an error.\n\n#### cleanup\n\nThe local `--cleanup | -c` flag instructs containerlab to remove the lab directory and all its content.\n\nWithout this flag present, containerlab will keep the lab directory and all files inside of it.\n\nWith `--runtime c9s`, `--cleanup` also deletes the lab's persistent node storage (the PersistentVolumeClaims holding saved device configuration) and then the lab namespace. A plain destroy keeps the claims, so the next deploy of the lab boots from the saved configuration. See [device state persistence](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#device-state-persistence).\n\nRefer to the [configuration artifacts](../manual/conf-artifacts.md) page to get more information on the lab directory contents.\n\n#### graceful\n\nTo make containerlab attempt a graceful shutdown of the running containers, add the `--graceful` flag to destroy cmd. Without it, containers will be removed forcefully without even attempting to stop them.\n\n#### keep-mgmt-net\n\nDo not try to remove the management network. Usually the management docker network (in case of docker) and the underlying bridge are being removed. If you have attached additional resources outside of containerlab and you want the bridge to remain intact just add the `--keep-mgmt-net` flag.\n\n#### all\n\nDestroy command provided with `--all | -a` flag will perform the deletion of all the labs running on the container host. It will not touch containers launched manually.\n\n#### yes\n\nThe `--yes | -y` flag can be used together with `--all` to auto-approve deletion of all labs, skipping the interactive confirmation prompt. This is useful for automation or scripting scenarios where manual confirmation is not desired.\n\n#### node-filter\n\nThe local `--node-filter` flag allows users to specify a subset of topology nodes targeted by `destroy` command. The value of this flag is a comma-separated list of node names as they appear in the topology.\n\nWhen a subset of nodes is specified, containerlab will only destroy those nodes and their links and leave the rest of the topology intact.  \nAs such, users can destroy a subset of nodes and links in a lab without destroying the entire topology.\n\nRead more about [node filtering](../manual/node-filtering.md) in the documentation.\n\n### Examples\n\n#### Destroy a lab described in the given topology file\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab destroy -t mylab.clab.yml\n```\n\n#### Destroy a lab and remove the Lab directory\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab destroy -t mylab.clab.yml --cleanup\n```\n\n#### Destroy a lab without specifying topology file\n\nGiven that a single topology file is present in the current directory.\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab destroy\n```\n\n#### Destroy all labs on the container host\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab destroy -a\n```\n\n#### Destroy all labs on the container host without confirmation prompt\n\n```bash\ncontainerlab destroy -a -y\n```\n\n#### Destroy a lab using short flag names\n\n```bash\nclab des\n```",

Reasoning
Confirmed the structure. Note: the destroy sweep at 497-509 uses state AFTER the destroy. Does anything delete the state file before this point (e.g., cleanup at end)? The sweep runs before lab-dir removal presumably. `c.deleteNodes` doesn't remove state. OK.

One important check on the sweep at line 507: `state.Topology.Nodes` — is it a map keyed by short name? clabtypes.Topology.Nodes is `map[string]*NodeDefinition` keyed by node name. Yes.

Also note the destroy-copy `c.Nodes` comes from `makeCopyForDestroy` rendering with CURRENT vars. If render fails (template error), destroy errors out — fine.

Now also note: `deleteLeftoverLabContainers` runs for the `--all` path? In the `--all` case, destroy is invoked per-lab via ListContainers... the code path I see is per-lab destroy with nodes defined → sweep applies per lab. Fine.

One more potential issue with `deleteLeftoverLabContainers`: it lists by lab name — includes containers whose node IS in the topology but under a different LONG name? `ownedByTopology[cfg.LongName]`; `cont.Names[0]` is the container name (long name). For regular nodes, LongName == container name. For bridge nodes — no containers. ext-container: LongName == ShortName (external container name) — external containers aren't labeled, never listed. Tailscale sidecars: they carry NodeName label of the owner node and... are they in c.Nodes? Tailscale sidecars are added as nodes (injectTailscaleSidecars adds them to c.Nodes? or as separate?). The ToolType label check (`cont.Labels[clabconstants.ToolType] != ""` → skip) covers tool containers regardless. OK.

Now — the `waitForParentContainer` infinite Created/Restarting/Removing: I decided coverage note.

Next, verify remaining unread parts of diff: lines 563-1303 (core/destroy network_mode_test, runtime_state.go, topology_reconcile.go hunks) — my summary says read, but let me spot-check the runtime_state.go BridgeNS hunk and topology_reconcile.go's deleteApplyEndpoints/migration skip at 1480 and removeDesertedBridgeDevices planning, plus apply.go orchestration (already verified). And the migration_test hunk 1303-1644. Let me read diff 563-940 and 940-1303 to be complete.

Mostly benign skip.

And `recoverParkedBridgeNSPorts` uses `isBridgeNSNode(nodeName)` which requires kind bridge — safe.

The realistic harm: RemoveDesertedBridge executing inside a node's container — a netns exec + LinkByName miss → nil. 361: }

363: // isOwnedBy reports whether link carries the ownership marker of the logical

365: // releases carry a marker for the bridge name of the mgmt-net link node instead
366: // of the stable mgmt-net owner name, and are accepted as well.
367: func isOwnedBy(link netlink.Link, node Node, ownerName, ifaceName string) bool {
368: 	if HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, ownerName, ifaceName) {
369: 		return true

372: 	if _, ok := node.(*mgmtBridgeLinkNode); ok && ownerName == mgmtNetOwnerName {
373: 		return HasOwnershipAltNameFor(link, node.GetShortName(), ifaceName)
374: 	}

Idempotent: if the port is already parked, returns the existing\n// relocation.\nfunc ParkBridgePortByOwnership(\n\tctx context.Context,\n\tsrc Node,\n\townerName string,\n\tifaceName string,\n\townerLongName string,\n) (*BridgePortRelocation, error) {\n\tparkPath, err := clabutils.CreateOrGetNamedNetNS(clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(ownerLongName))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"failed to create parking netns for migration: %w\", err)\n\t}\n\n\trelocation := &BridgePortRelocation{\n\t\tparkNSPath:   parkPath,\n\t\tOldOwnerName: ownerName,\n\t\tIfaceName:    ifaceName,\n\t\tLongName:     ownerLongName,\n\t}\n\n\t// Idempotency: a previous apply may have parked the port and failed before\n\t// restoring it. Reasoning
One notable subtlety in `removeOwnedInterfaceStrict` (line 299): `netlink.LinkByName(clabutils.SanitizeInterfaceName(ifaceName))` — for BridgeNS deletes, `ref.key.iface` is the LOGICAL name (or kernel name for orphans). For matched endpoints, the logical name may exceed 15 chars so the kernel name differs (e.g. `c1eth1` fits; but a logical name like `client1-ethernet-iface` → sanitized kernel name `cl_...hash`). For orphan keys, key.iface is the KERNEL name — `SanitizeInterfaceName(kernelName)` — does sanitize alter an already-sanitized name? SanitizeInterfaceName presumably truncates/hashes names >15 chars; a kernel name is ≤15, but sanitize may also replace invalid chars (kernel names wouldn't have them). Probably idempotent-ish for kernel names ≤ 15 chars. For matched endpoints deletion (non-migration stale BridgeNS endpoints with logical names >15 chars): LinkByName(sanitized(logical)) — sanitized(logical) IS how the kernel name was created → matches. OK consistent.

`RemoveDesertedBridge`: LinkByName miss → nil. Benign. Confirmed.

Now, let me check `parkedKernelNameFor` and the restore path remainder (migration.go 150-371) — mostly read. Also verify the ownership altname helper `HasOwnershipAltNameFor` uses sha1 hash — fine.

Remaining: skim the migration test (diff 1303-1644) and apply.go orchestration diff (1-398) — I verified apply order earlier from head file core/apply.go. Let me now skim the migration test quickly for coverage assessment.

But those were just deleted by deleteNodes, so they wouldn't be in the list anyway. Hmm, but if a node's container failed to delete in deleteNodes... Actually the sweep lists containers AFTER deleteNodes. If deleteNodes failed to delete a rendered node's container (error path), the sweep would delete it anyway — arguably fine for destroy semantics.

Actually wait — the real question is whether the sweep is meant to EXCLUDE rendered nodes. Let me re-check the sweep code: it enumerates lab-labeled containers, and skips those whose `Names[0]` is in `ownedByTopology` (built from c.Nodes LongNames) and skips state-entry ones. So it's designed to only delete "leftover" containers. If `Names[0]` has a leading `/`, the exclusion never triggers, and the sweep deletes everything lab-labeled that's not a tool. For destroy, that's behaviorally near-identical (rendered containers were already deleted). So the severity of a leading-slash issue is low — it makes the exclusion dead code but doesn't break destroy semantics. But it WOULD matter if deleteNodes deliberately skipped something... no, deleteNodes deletes everything rendered.

Reasoning
Docker runtime trims leading `/` from names (`strings.TrimLeft(n, "/")` at docker.go:1565), so `cont.Names[0]` matches `cfg.LongName`. Podman: `runtime/podman/util.go:457` `Names: v.Names` — podman names don't carry a leading slash (podman returns bare names). OK, the `ownedByTopology[cont.Names[0]]` lookup works. Good, no finding.

Investigation is now complete. Let me compose the final review with the findings:

**Finding 1 (P3):** Hardcoded `clab-%s-%s` long-name derivation in `core/destroy.go:507` (state-entry sweep) and `core/apply_bridge_migration.go:46` (`bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` fallback) diverges from prefix-aware `nodeLongName` (config.go:309) when `prefix` is `__lab-name`, custom, or empty. Scenarios:
- Custom/`__lab-name` prefix + bridge move (common apply flow): park keys use the hardcoded fallback (stale bridge absent from `c.Nodes`), while recovery in the next apply (`recoverParkedBridgeNSPorts`) keys by `cfg.LongName` of the desired bridge. Mismatch → recovery misses the parked port → client pair deleted/recreated instead of migrated; parked netns half orphaned.
- Destroy sweep: state-entry names hardcoded; with custom prefix, parking netns parked under `cfg.LongName` (rendered at park time) doesn't match the hardcoded sweep name → leftover named netns mount.

Suggested correction: single helper deriving long name with the running prefix (`nodeLongName`-equivalent taking `c.Config.Prefix`), used by `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` fallback and the destroy sweep state entries.

**Finding 2 (P4):** Empty parking netns leaks when the owner bridge leaves both rendered topology and state. `UnlinkEmptyParkingNetNS` is only called from `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` (apply_bridge_migration.go:124); if a migration is interrupted (parked port) and the owner bridge is subsequently removed from the topology by a successful apply, the state is rewritten without the bridge, and neither the destroy-time parking-netns sweep (drives names only from `c.Nodes` + state) nor any apply path can derive `ParkingNetnsName` → empty bind-mounted netns persists on the host. Fix: record parking netns name (or owner long name) in `LabState` at park time, or sweep `clab-park-*` netnses by lab-name suffix.

With default prefix, owner long name contains the lab name, so a suffix-based sweep by lab name would work. The current sweep enumerates candidate names from rendered+state nodes only. OK.

Reasoning
All anchors confirmed. Investigation complete. Now compose the final review.

Findings:

**Finding 1 — P3:** Hardcoded `clab-%s-%s` long-name derivation diverges from `nodeLongName` under non-default prefixes.
- Locations: `core/apply_bridge_migration.go:40-47` (head) and `core/destroy.go:506-508` (head); root cause contrast with `core/config.go:309-318`.
- Problem: Both derive the bridge node's container long name as `clab-<lab>-<node>`, but the actual long name depends on `prefix`: `__lab-name` → `<lab>-<node>`, custom → `<prefix>-<lab>-<node>`, empty → `<node>`. In the common bridge-move case, the stale bridge node is absent from `c.Nodes` (it was removed from the desired topology), so `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` falls back to the hardcoded form — this is the primary path, not an edge. Parking keys, recovery lookups (`recoverParkedBridgeNSPorts` via `ParkingNetnsName(node.Config().LongName)` in `topology_reconcile.go:1098`), and the destroy sweep state entries all use these derivations.
- Trigger: deploy with `prefix: __lab-name` (or a custom/empty prefix), perform a bridge move (`br01|bp1` → `br01|bp2`); the interrupted-migration recovery, or destroy after parking, computes a different key than the one the park step used.
- Impact: with a non-default prefix, an interrupted migration's parked port is not recovered on the next apply (link is deleted/recreated instead — functional but defeats the migration feature and drops the client pair), and the destroy-time parking-netns sweep computes the wrong `ParkingNetnsName` for state-recorded nodes, leaving the bind-mounted parking netns on the host. With the default `clab` prefix all derivations coincide, so default-prefix users are unaffected.
- Suggestion: route both derivations through `c.nodeLongName(nodeName)` (the prefix-aware helper at `core/config.go:309`), which produces exactly the default form when the prefix is `clab`; optionally add a unit test with `prefix: __lab-name`.

Note the fallback in `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` is documented as "the standard clab-<lab>-<node> derivation" — the fix is small and at the root.

**Finding 2 — P4:** Empty parking netns leaks when the owner bridge leaves both the rendered topology and the lab state.
- Location: `core/apply_bridge_migration.go:49-64` (comment claims destroy sweeps abandoned entries) + `links/migration.go:324` (`UnlinkEmptyParkingNetNS` only invoked from `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts`).
- Trigger: migration interrupted between park and restore → subsequent apply removes the bridge node from the topology entirely (successful, rewrites state without the bridge) → destroy. Neither `c.Nodes` nor `state.Topology.Nodes` contains the owner, so `SweepParkingNetnses` never derives its `ParkingNetnsName`.
- Impact: an empty named netns (bind mount) persists on the host; harmless but leaks until manually removed. Low frequency (requires interrupted migration followed by bridge removal).
- Suggestion: persist the parking netns name (or owner long name) into `LabState` when parking, or have the sweep also consider `clab-park-*` names matching the lab name.

**Finding 3 — P4 (docs):** `docs/cmd/destroy.md` does not document the new destroy behavior.
- The destroy path now (a) deletes lab-labeled containers absent from the rendered topology (`deleteLeftoverLabContainers`, `core/destroy.go:455`), and (b) sweeps parking netnses for the lab's nodes (`core/destroy.go:485-513`). Neither is reflected in `docs/cmd/destroy.md`.
- Impact: users deploying with vars that remove nodes previously had to `destroy`/`deploy` fully to clear leftovers; the new sweep changes observable destroy behavior (removes containers not in the given topology file) but is undocumented, so users can't rely on or predict it.
- Suggestion: add a short paragraph to `docs/cmd/destroy.md` describing both sweeps, mirroring the wording of the code comments.

- `waitForParentContainer` unbounded-poll concern resolved: both deploy (`waitForNodeDeployTarget` gates dependents on Running parents) and apply (`waitForApplyNetworkModeTarget`) paths guarantee parents Running before dependents start; external parents are rejected by the `dp.Nodes` membership check; `Stopped` errors out. Remaining statuses unreachable in practice.
- `strings.Contains(name, "|")` heuristics (`planDesertedBridgeDeviceRemovals`, state-link detection) can only misfire on non-bridge nodes whose names contain `|`; the schema allowed `|` before this PR, but container names with `|` are rejected by the runtimes, so such nodes never deploy — heuristic is safe in practice.

# Code Review: In-container bridges (`network-mode: container:`) with destroy-time sweeps

This PR adds "BridgeNS" bridges — bridge nodes placed inside a parent container via `network-mode: container:<parent>` with name-encoded `<bridge>|<parent>` nodes — including link migration through parking netnses, deserted-bridge-device cleanup, and destroy-time leftover-container/parking-netns sweeps. The design is coherent: dependency ordering (`deploy.go`/`apply.go`) gates dependents on running parents, migration guards are conservative, and the recovery paths are well-commented and tested. I found no blocking defects. Three lower-severity issues follow, all rooted in the same pattern: hardcoding the container long-name derivation instead of reusing the prefix-aware helper.

## Summary

| # | Severity | Title |
|---|----------|-------|
| 1 | P3 | Hardcoded `clab-%s-%s` long-name derivation breaks bridge-port parking/recovery/sweep under non-default `prefix` |
| 2 | P4 | Empty parking netns leaks when the owner bridge leaves both the topology and the lab state |
| 3 | P4 | New destroy sweeps (leftover containers, parking netnses) are not documented in `docs/cmd/destroy.md` |

## Findings

### 1. P3 — Hardcoded `clab-%s-%s` long-name derivation breaks bridge-port parking/recovery/sweep under non-default `prefix`

**Location:** [`core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L40-L47`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L40-L47) and [`core/destroy.go#L497-L509`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L497-L509) (head)

**Problem:** Both sites derive a bridge node's container long name as `fmt.Sprintf("clab-%s-%s", ...)` instead of reusing the prefix-aware [`nodeLongName`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/config.go#L309-L318) helper, which yields `<lab>-<node>` for `prefix: __lab-name`, `<prefix>-<lab>-<node>` for a custom prefix, and the bare node name for an empty prefix. The fallback in `bridgeNSMigOwnerLongName` is not an edge case: in the common bridge-move flow the stale bridge node is intentionally absent from `c.Nodes`, so parking keys the netns by the hardcoded form. Recovery on the next apply (`recoverParkedBridgeNSPorts` via `ParkingNetnsName(node.Config().LongName)` at `core/topology_reconcile.go:1098`) and the destroy-time state-entry sweep then compute a different key than the one parking used.

**Trigger:** Deploy a lab with `prefix: __lab-name` (or a custom/empty prefix) and move a bridge between parents (`br01|bp1` → `br01|bp2`). If the migration is interrupted between park and restore, the next apply's recovery lookup and a later destroy's `SweepParkingNetnses` derive names that do not match the parked key.

**Impact:** With non-default prefixes, an interrupted migration's parked port is not recovered; the client pair is deleted and recreated instead (functional, but the migration feature silently degrades to a full link teardown), and the destroy sweep leaves the bind-mounted parking netns on the host. Default-prefix (`clab`) users are unaffected because all derivations coincide — which is also why the smoke test passes.

**Correction:** Route both derivations through `c.nodeLongName(nodeName)`, which reproduces the current `clab` form exactly for default deployments. Optionally add a unit test exercising the fallback path with `prefix: __lab-name`.

### 2. P4 — Empty parking netns leaks when the owner bridge leaves both the topology and the lab state

**Location:** [`core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L49-L64`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/apply_bridge_migration.go#L49-L64) (head), with `UnlinkEmptyParkingNetNS` (`links/migration.go:324`) invoked only from `restoreMigratedBridgeNSPorts` (`core/apply_bridge_migration.go:124`)

**Problem:** The comment at this location states that parking entries abandoned by interrupted migrations are removed at destroy, "parked ports included," and the destroy sweep indeed enumerates both `c.Nodes` and `state.Topology.Nodes`. However, if a migration is interrupted between park and restore and a subsequent successful apply removes the bridge node entirely, that apply rewrites the lab state without the bridge. At destroy time neither source can derive the owner's `ParkingNetnsName`, and no apply path unlinks the now-empty netns because the only `UnlinkEmptyParkingNetNS` call site is the successful-restore path.

**Trigger:** Interrupt a bridge move (parked half sitting in `clab-park-...`), then apply a topology revision that deletes the bridge, then run `clab destroy` with the topology file.

**Impact:** An empty named network namespace (bind mount) persists on the host indefinitely. Harmless to subsequent labs, purely a host-hygiene leak, and requires an unlikely event sequence.

**Correction:** Record the parking netns name (or the owner's long name) in `LabState` at park time so the destroy sweep can enumerate it, or extend the sweep to match `clab-park-*` entries containing the lab name.

### 3. P4 — New destroy sweeps are not documented in `docs/cmd/destroy.md`

**Location:** Change in [`core/destroy.go#L455`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L455) and [`core/destroy.go#L485-L513`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/ce5f7036a6ad0aeceb4313ce84ae61844c885d07/core/destroy.go#L485-L513) (head); missing counterpart in `docs/cmd/destroy.md`

**Problem:** Destroy now (a) deletes lab-labeled containers absent from the rendered topology via `deleteLeftoverLabContainers` — covering containers removed by vars-driven deploys — and (b) sweeps parking netnses for all deploy nodes plus state-recorded nodes. Neither behavior appears in `docs/cmd/destroy.md`, while the PR does document the related deploy and bridge-kind behavior in `docs/cmd/deploy.md` and `docs/manual/kinds/bridge.md`.

**Trigger:** A user reads the destroy docs to learn what `clab destroy -t <file>` removes.

**Impact:** Users cannot rely on or predict the new cleanup behavior; they may keep doing full destroy/deploy cycles to clear leftover containers that destroy now handles automatically, or be surprised that containers not in the supplied topology file are removed.

**Correction:** Add a short paragraph to `docs/cmd/destroy.md` describing both sweeps, mirroring the wording of the code comments at `core/destroy.go:485-489`.

## Coverage notes

- **Source-only review.** Tests were not executed; all findings derive from reading the diff, surrounding callers, helpers, schemas, docs, and tests in the snapshot.
- `waitForParentContainer` in `nodes/bridge/bridge.go` polls some container statuses without a bound, but both deploy (`waitForNodeDeployTarget`) and apply (`waitForApplyNetworkModeTarget`) paths gate dependents on Running parents first, external parents are rejected by the `dp.Nodes` membership check, and `Stopped` parents error out — the unbounded statuses are unreachable in practice, so no finding is raised.
- The `strings.Contains(name, "|")` heuristics in `planDesertedBridgeDeviceRemovals` and the state-link detection can only misfire on non-bridge nodes whose names contain `|`; the schema already allowed `|` at the merge base, but runtimes reject `|` in container names, so such nodes never deploy and the heuristic is safe in practice.
- Leftover-sweep name matching was verified against runtime normalization: docker trims the leading `/` in `produceGenericContainerList` (`runtime/docker/docker.go:1562-1566`), and podman returns bare names.
- The fd-handle usage in `nodes/bridge/bridge.go`'s `ExecFunction`/`GetNSPath` matches the existing `DefaultNode` precedent; the CLI process is short-lived, so impact is negligible.
- Owned-but-detached veth ends (not mastered by the bridge) are invisible to orphan discovery, which only collects interfaces with `MasterIndex == bridgeIndex`; this is a minor edge leak predating the sweep design.
- Interface names longer than 15 characters skip migration (logical vs kernel name comparison) and fall back to delete/recreate — graceful.
- Test coverage is solid for planning logic (`core/topology_reconcile_migration_test.go` guard and deserted-device tables) and end-to-end flows (smoke test 34 covers move, parent drift, interrupted-recovery injection, bridge removal, and idempotency). Two gaps remain untested: the destroy leftover-container sweep (teardown uses `destroy --name`, which takes the `deleteContainersDirect` branch) and any non-default-`prefix` scenario, which is exactly where Finding 1 lives.
